name: Qserv
tagline: Distributed shared-nothing SQL database built to serve the Rubin Observatory's petascale sky catalogs.
description: Qserv is the catalog database of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (LSST), developed at SLAC for more than a decade. A front-end 'czar' accepts MySQL-protocol queries, rewrites them into many per-chunk sub-queries and fans them out over XRootD to worker nodes that each run MariaDB on their slice of the data; results are merged and returned. Tables are partitioned spatially into sky chunks with a director table (such as Object) that keeps related rows co-located, so near-neighbour and object-to-source joins run without moving data. The SQL dialect is restricted (no subqueries, writes go through a separate ingest service) but adds spherical-geometry predicates via scisql. It is actively developed, but it is a purpose-built science system rather than a general database.
developer: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory / Vera C. Rubin Observatory

scale.notes: Built to hold the multi-billion-object Rubin catalogs across many worker nodes; spatial chunks with overlap let near-neighbour joins run without data movement.

strengths: Spatial chunking keeps related rows together so astronomy joins stay local to a worker
Fans one SQL query out to thousands of chunk queries in parallel
Speaks the MySQL protocol, so standard clients and TAP services connect directly
Director index gives fast lookups by object ID across the whole catalog
Open source and actively developed for a flagship survey
weaknesses: Restricted SQL: no subqueries, strict rules on spatial predicates and ORDER BY
Data is loaded through a dedicated ingest workflow, not ordinary INSERT/UPDATE
Small, domain-specific community; documentation assumes astronomy catalogs
useCases: Serving petascale astronomical object and source catalogs
Spatial cone and box searches over sky surveys
Large read-mostly scientific tables partitioned by position
notIdealFor: General-purpose analytics outside spatially partitioned data
Small teams wanting a turnkey warehouse
